articles.title: Is Qwen Code Really Free? A Practical Setup and Pricing Guide (2026)
articles.excerpt: Qwen Code is an open-source AI coding agent that can inspect repositories, edit files, execute commands, and connect to different AI model providers. But there's a question that often causes confusion…
articles.body: Qwen Code is an open-source AI coding agent that can inspect repositories, edit files, execute commands, and connect to different AI model providers. But there's a question that often causes confusion: Is Qwen Code actually free, or do you need to pay for an API key? The short answer: the client is free, but the AI models you connect to it may not be. And if you're following an older tutorial that recommends signing in with Qwen OAuth for free usage, that advice is now outdated. Here's how Qwen Code works in 2026 and how to set it up without choosing the wrong authentication or billing method. 1. What is free, and what costs money? Qwen Code itself is an open-source application licensed under Apache 2.0. You can install the client without purchasing a software license.

articles.title: Let Claude Code query your database read only with the DBX MCP server
articles.excerpt: Coding agents guess at database schemas. You can paste the schema into the chat, or you can hand the agent raw credentials and hope. The second option is the risky one. DBX is a database client (deskt…
articles.body: Coding agents guess at database schemas. You can paste the schema into the chat, or you can hand the agent raw credentials and hope. The second option is the risky one. DBX is a database client (desktop, Docker, CLI and web) that advertises 100+ databases in 25 MB, and it ships an MCP server. That lets Claude Code or Cursor inspect real tables through DBX, limited to the connections you allow and set to read only. Set up Install DBX and add your database connections in the app. Check that the MCP server starts: npx @dbx-app/mcp-server Add a dbx entry to your project's .mcp.json , using npx as the command and -y @dbx-app/mcp-server as the args: { "mcpServers" : { "dbx" : { "command" : "npx" , "args" : [ "-y" , "@dbx-app/mcp-server" ] } } } In DBX, open Settings, then MCP.

articles.title: Cut tokens on AI code reviews with code-review-graph
articles.excerpt: When you ask Claude Code, Codex or Cursor to review a change in a big repo, the agent usually does one of two things. It reads far too many files and burns your context window, or it reads too few and…
articles.body: When you ask Claude Code, Codex or Cursor to review a change in a big repo, the agent usually does one of two things. It reads far too many files and burns your context window, or it reads too few and misses the caller your change breaks. Neither is a great way to spend tokens. code-review-graph takes a different route. It parses your codebase with Tree-sitter into a local graph of functions, classes, imports, calls and test coverage, then serves a small slice of that graph to your assistant over MCP. The assistant reads only the files a change actually touches. The README reports about 63x fewer tokens per question at the median across six repos. We have not reproduced that number ourselves, so treat it as the author's benchmark.

articles.title: Building an In-Memory Circuit Breaker for Webhook Ingress: Shedding Load Without Losing Events
articles.excerpt: Webhooks connect cloud systems. Payment providers like Stripe, code hosts like GitHub and commerce platforms like Shopify all use them to tell your services that something changed. When a sender has a…
articles.body: Webhooks connect cloud systems. Payment providers like Stripe, code hosts like GitHub and commerce platforms like Shopify all use them to tell your services that something changed. When a sender has a bad day, you pay for it. A bulk export, a backfill or a burst of retries can hit your ingress endpoint, and the endpoint is the first thing that fails. When a burst arrives, worker threads or goroutines block on slow downstream calls and connection pools saturate. Memory fills with queued request bodies and garbage-collection pressure pushes latency higher. Health checks start failing, the load balancer moves traffic to the remaining nodes, and those nodes tip over too. This guide describes an in-memory admission controller for webhook ingress.

articles.title: Converting Excel Worksheets to Images in Java: A Practical Look
articles.excerpt: Excel workbooks are designed for data manipulation and analysis, but there are scenarios where a static image is more appropriate. Whether you are generating report snapshots for a web dashboard, embe…
articles.body: Excel workbooks are designed for data manipulation and analysis, but there are scenarios where a static image is more appropriate. Whether you are generating report snapshots for a web dashboard, embedding table data into an email, or archiving records in a format that prevents accidental edits, converting worksheets to images is a practical requirement. In Java, this task is not natively supported by the standard library. While Apache POI is the de facto standard for reading and writing Excel files, it does not include a rendering engine to produce visual output. This is where third-party libraries come into play. This article examines the practical aspects of converting Excel content to images in a Java environment using Spire.XLS for Java as an example tool.

articles.body: A vulnerability in the WordPress Core update process involves predictable staging paths that are accessible through the web during upgrades. According to Defiant, the race condition can be exploited without authentication and could lead to remote code execution. Attack complexity is rated high, so remote accessibility alone does not establish that exploitation will succeed. Patch and technical scope The vulnerability was patched on October 28 in WordPress 7.1.4, with fixes backported to branches from WordPress 4.7 onward. It has not yet been assigned a CVE ID. The patch randomizes staging directories, adds index protection, and prevents unsafe handling of staging configuration data. These changes address directory predictability and staging data handling.

articles.body: For more information, contact Joel W. Sills, Langley Research Center, joel.w.sills@nasa.gov . Download the PDF version An instrumented hammer test does not require an idealized single half-sine waveform. When the complete force and response are measured accurately, crest ripples and separated contacts remain known inputs. Force shape changes excitation, but does not inherently invalidate the record. Adequacy depends on measurement accuracy, bandwidth, signal-to-noise ratio, and coverage of the test objective. Background: What the Hammer Actually Measures Hammer tests support modal analysis [2–4] and can precede pyroshock testing [6]. articles.title: New 'Star Trek: The Original Voyages' book traces the stellar legacy of the bold sci-fi brand
articles.excerpt: Keep the 60th anniversary party going with this visual salute to the series that launched a legacy
articles.body: "Star Trek" celebrated its diamond anniversary last month, marking 60 years since it first aired on NBC on Sept. 8, 1966. There were a bunch of Trekkie-themed celebrations and news stories over September, including festive documentaries , special screenings , tributes, parade floats , interviews, and even a Galileo shuttle story. Now, publishers Penguin Random House and Ten Speed Press are releasing " Star Trek: The Original Voyages: A Visual History " on Nov. 10, 2026. This coffee table book promises unprecedented exploration of the pioneering space fantasy television series and enduring pop culture property that bolstered the space race and ignited sci-fi audiences' imaginations by taking us to strange new worlds and civilizations in the final frontier.

articles.title: Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.8 II EVO FE (APO) lens review — how good is this budget lens for astrophotography?
articles.excerpt: The Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.8 II FE (APO) is an inexpensive prime that works well for astrophotography thanks to its focal length and maximum aperture.
articles.body: Key specs Type: Full-frame prime lens Focal length: 35 mm Maximum aperture: f/1.8 Lens mount: Sony FE & Nikon Z Weight: 12.52 oz / 355 g Dimensions: 3.33 x 4.37 in / 69 x 76 mm Filter thread: 58 mm Release date: April 2026 Budget primes can be, surprisingly, excellent choices for photographers shooting all subjects. It’s all too easy to get carried away with the best specs, such as a large maximum aperture and impressive optical design often seen in more expensive options. But affordable lenses like the Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.8 II FE (APO) have the potential to impress and delight in equal measure. The 35mm f/1.8 is a compact and lightweight lens offering a reasonably fast maximum aperture, making it a prime candidate for astrophotography.

articles.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Crew “Returns” to Earth
articles.excerpt: The four-member Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) crew poses outside for the first time in more than a year following the end of their simulated Mars journey on Oct. 31, 2026. Cr…
articles.body: NASA/James Blair The four-member Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) crew poses outside for the first time in more than a year following the end of their simulated Mars journey on Oct. 31, 2026. Crew members Matthew Montgomery (left), James Spicer (middle left), Ross Elder (middle right), and Ellen Ellis (right) spent more than a year testing systems, maintaining crops, managing limited resources and communication delays, conducting extravehicular activities and more in efforts to help NASA better understand how crews adapt to long-duration stays. Insights from their experiences will help NASA design its future Moon Base and plan for missions on Mars. Image credit: NASA/James Blair

articles.body: A botnet of more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes, lost control of its servers in late October in a takedown led by Google.
